skill.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
skill.description: Coordinate multiple AI agents to investigate independent coding failures in parallel, then review and integrate their results.
skill.summary: Dispatch focused agents for independent debugging tasks and integrate their fixes safely.

content.value_statement: Independent failures waste time when one assistant investigates them sequentially. This skill helps you split work across focused agents and integrate results safely.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when failures are independent enough for parallel investigation.
Guides users to group failures by test file, subsystem, or bug domain.
Provides a structure for focused agent tasks with scope, goal, constraints, and expected output.
Shows how to dispatch multiple Claude Code tasks concurrently.
Defines review steps for summaries, conflicts, full test runs, and spot checks.
limitations: It works best when failures have separate root causes and separate files.
It does not merge changes or resolve conflicts automatically.
It depends on the user to provide accurate errors, constraints, and context.
It is focused on coding and test debugging workflows.

use_cases.title: Triage independent test failures
use_cases.description: Split unrelated failing test files into separate investigations and review the returned fixes together.

use_cases.title: Coordinate multi-agent debugging
use_cases.description: Create focused tasks for several Claude Code agents when each agent can work without shared state.

use_cases.title: Review parallel fix results
use_cases.description: Check agent summaries, identify conflicts, run the full suite, and spot check likely weak areas.

prompt_templates.title: Find split candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failing tests and tell me which failures are independent enough for separate agents. Group them by file or subsystem and explain any dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Draft focused tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Create clear prompts for each agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these independent failures into focused agent tasks. For each task, include scope, goal, constraints, required context, and expected summary.

prompt_templates.title: Plan parallel dispatch
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a parallel dispatch plan for these failures. Assign one agent per independent domain and note what each agent must avoid touching.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate agent results
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review after several agents return.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these agent summaries and propose an integration sequence. Identify conflicts, missing verification, and the final test commands I should run.

output_examples.input: Three unrelated test files fail after a refactor.
output_examples.output: The skill groups failures by file, assigns one focused investigation per file, and asks each agent for root cause and fix summary.

output_examples.input: Several agents return fixes from separate debugging tasks.
output_examples.output: The skill guides a review of summaries, overlapping edits, full-suite verification, and targeted spot checks before accepting changes.

output_examples.input: A user is unsure whether failures should be split.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a single investigation when failures share state, require full-system context, or may be fixed by one root cause.

best_practices: Use parallel agents only after confirming the failures are independent.
Give each agent one scope, one goal, explicit constraints, and required output.
Review all returned changes together and run the full test suite before integration.
anti_patterns: Do not dispatch agents when one fix may resolve every failure.
Do not give broad prompts such as fixing all tests without boundaries.
Do not accept parallel changes without checking conflicts and verification gaps.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when three or more coding failures are independent and can be investigated without shared state.

faq.question: Does it run agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and prompt structure for dispatching agents in Claude Code or similar tools.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The planning, task scoping, review, and integration guidance can support Codex workflows.

faq.question: What should each agent receive?
faq.answer: Each agent should receive one focused scope, relevant errors, constraints, and the summary expected on return.

faq.question: What are the main risks?
faq.answer: Agents may edit overlapping files, miss shared root causes, or return incomplete fixes without final review.

faq.question: How do I verify the results?
faq.answer: Read each summary, check for conflicts, run the full suite, and spot check areas likely to share behavior.
